race_context: Michigan City Area Schools (MCAS) runs 11 K-12 schools: Michigan City High School, Barker and Krueger middle schools and eight elementary schools. It also runs LaPorte County Career & Technical Education, the Little Wolves Early Learning Center and adult education {mcas_leadership}. Its board seats are named for the Civil City, Coolspring/Pine townships and Michigan/Springfield townships, plus one at-large seat, and the state ballot list shows the Civil City race in LaPorte and Porter counties {mcas_board}{in_list}. No current enrollment figure was found on the district pages reviewed; the district cites declining enrollment {mcas_ref}.
The superintendent is Dr. Wendel McCollum, who took the job on Aug. 5, 2024 {mcas_leadership}.

The board has seven members: four Civil City seats, one Coolspring/Pine Township seat, one Michigan/Springfield Township seat and one at-large seat {mcas_board}. Meetings are held on the last Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m., with different dates in November and December {mcas_board}.

Civil City seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list says vote for 1, but the Civil City race elects three members. County candidate lists show 'Vote for 3' for this race in 2018 and 2022, and the fourth Civil City seat was elected alone in 2024 {lpc_2018res}{lpc_2022cand}{lpc_2024res}{in_list}. The three Civil City members elected in 2022 were Thomas R. Dombkowski, Michael J. Gresham and Jenilee Haynes Peterson, chosen from four candidates; the district lists their terms as 2023-2026 {lpc_2022cand}{mcas_board}. Gresham and Haynes Peterson are running again. Dombkowski, the board's vice president, is not on the 2026 list {mcas_board}{in_list}.

Because the state list shows three different people for the Civil City race (Haynes Peterson's name appears twice), three candidates are running for what county records indicate are three seats {in_list}{lpc_2022cand}.

The fourth Civil City seat belongs to board president Marty Corley, Michigan City's police chief. He won it in November 2024 over Rodney McCormick, 60.8% to 39.2%, and was sworn in in January 2025, so his seat is not on the 2026 ballot {lpc_2024res}{hd_welcome}. The district's web page still lists his term as '2021-2026' {mcas_board}.

At-large seat (one seat): at-large member Phyllis Stark resigned in July 2025 {nwi_stark}. On Sept. 29, 2025, the board voted unanimously to appoint Vera Gaston to the seat {hd_gaston}. The district lists Gaston's term as 2025-2026, and she is running against Michelle Lynn Duck {mcas_board}{in_list}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Porter and LaPorte county school board candidates could file under a political party {nwi_parties}. In this district, the state list shows Duck and Gillespie as Independent, Gresham as Democratic, and Gaston and Haynes Peterson as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Operating referendum: on June 30, 2026, the board voted to put an eight-year operating referendum on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot {hd_refboard}{nwi_ref80}. The district says the maximum rate would be about $0.2998 per $100 of assessed value, or about $260 a year on a home with a $200,000 median assessed value, through 2034 {mcas_ref}. The NWI Times describes it as an $80 million referendum {nwi_ref80}. The district says the money would pay for student programs, transportation, safety, staff recruitment and retention, and student behavior and health services, and could not be used for construction {mcas_ref}.

Budget and SEA 1: MCAS projects about $2.56 million less revenue over three years than it had expected, because of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) and the tax caps {mcas_finance}. It says it has already cut about $3 million in spending and has eliminated positions or left them vacant {mcas_finance}. The district says it currently has no referendum fund {mcas_ref}. It held community meetings and launched a school-finance video series ahead of the vote {nwi_refmeet}{hd_finvideo}.

Facilities: on May 26, 2026, the board unanimously approved three resolutions for a bond project covering elementary school renovations, HVAC work and a new athletic facility. Gresham made the motion {hd_bonds}. Construction of a new track and turf field started in May 2026 {hd_sports}. On July 28, 2026, the board approved a $182 million long-term facilities and grade-configuration plan that turns Krueger Middle School into a grades 5-8 intermediate school {nwi_config}{hd_facilities}.
Staff: in October 2025 the board considered a new collective bargaining agreement with the Michigan City Education Association {hd_contract}.

Forums: no 2026 school board forum or candidate questionnaire for this district was found. The League of Women Voters of La Porte County announced two general-election candidate forums, but the coverage reviewed does not say whether school board candidates were included {hd_lwv}.
Coverage of these candidates is sparse. The main local daily, the Herald-Dispatch, and the NWI Times are paywalled, and only the openings of their articles could be read.

review_flags.person: Michigan City Area Schools (district employee, not a candidate)
review_flags.summary: Hometown News Now reported on Oct. 5, 2026 that a Michigan City Area Schools employee faces one Level 6 felony fraud count, filed in July 2025, over alleged personal use of $3,986.11 in district funds. The State Board of Accounts reported in late August 2026 that MCAS lacked proper internal controls over some financial policies. The district's business manager acknowledged the findings and listed eight corrective actions. The employee resigned May 6, 2025, and a hearing was set for Oct. 26 in La Porte Superior Court 4. The case is unresolved {htn_sboa}.
review_flags.note: This concerns a district employee, not a candidate. It may matter for board oversight of finances during the referendum campaign. The charge is unresolved. No candidate statement on the audit findings was found. Editor: relevant as a district-level overview item (top of the district's ballot section), not a candidate item. Further study: identify who oversees the area involved (board members and administrators responsible for finance/internal controls) and how the board responded to the audit.
